keyFindings.description: BLOCKING. The issue's roles now share one bun install cache (manifest.go:734), and a cold fill of that cache is not concurrency-safe — so the daemon's own rendered plugin install can fail a role's launch. Reproduced at this head in this reviewer's container with the image's bun 1.3.14: six concurrent `bun add --backend=copyfile --exact chalk@5.3.0 lodash@4.17.21` into six separate directories against one empty BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR on the issue's volume left five of six at exit 1 ('ENOENT: failed copying files from cache to destination for package lodash', 'Failed to install 1 package'); the same six against the now-warm cache were 6/6 exit 0, so the race is the cold entry fill, not the install out of it. Before this push the cache was per role, and before the branch it was unset and fell back to the container's own filesystem, so no two roles ever filled one cache. installScript takes `|| { echo ...; exit 1; }` on a failed `bun add` (plugins.go:112), so the role's agent never execs and the launch fails. The trigger is routine rather than exotic: an installing launch renders this install for every role of a kept pod whose recorded contract differs from the daemon's, and a plugin-version bump makes the pair cold for all of them at once. This is not a reversal of the human's decision — the fix is a lock or a retry around the one install Legion renders, plus the hazard stated where the Playwright one already is (docs/kubernetes.md:1797-1804, which does exactly this analysis for the neighbouring tool).

The doc comment on the function that performs the feature still states the rule this push deleted: 'then the directories environ's TMPDIR, cache and data homes and Go and bun caches name, on the role's own scratch but the two Go caches, which the issue's roles share'. It is exactly backwards now — only XDG_STATE_HOME is the role's own and the Go pair is no more shared than the other four — and it sits directly above the podsafety.EnsureScratch call, which is the first place a maintainer reads to learn what is shared. `jj diff --from 74675db54cc7 --to daddf9c2c271 packages/daemon/cmd/legion/` is empty: the file was never touched this round. Two more of the same class: plugins.go:92 still says 'the role's bun install cache', and claude-envoy's published CHANGELOG.md:58 says the Go caches are 'the pair on that volume they already were', which contract entry 33 contradicts on the same page — at 32 the runtime set neither GOCACHE nor GOMODCACHE, so they are new names, as version.go:254 says. 'Already were' is true only of earlier rounds of this branch, which no reader of a published changelog can see.

The only paragraph that tells an operator how to size issue_volume puts the ~400 MB Playwright Chromium under the per-role state home — 'One directory is the role's own, its state home at /legion/scratch/state/<role>, with a Playwright Chromium under it about 400 MB' — and then tells the operator at :1207 that the arithmetic is 'one set of four, one Go pair, and one state home per role the issue runs'. So the reader multiplies 400 MB by the roles for something now stored once. Line 1842 of the same document, added by this push, says the opposite and is right: sharing the cache home gives the issue's roles one Playwright registry, since playwright-core resolves it from XDG_CACHE_HOME. The implementer's own recorded measurement agrees with 1842 (implement.json proof entry 2 observed the install under .../cache/ms-playwright). The state home holds Oh My Pi's logs, Chromium's browser-profiles and the installed plugin generation (manifest.go:751-753), not the downloaded browser. This is the same failure the last two rounds corrected once each in this same paragraph.

Merging the two scratch tests dropped one assertion pair, and only for the directory with a stated correctness mechanism behind it. The deleted TestEachRoleIsToldAScratchDirectoryOfItsOwnOnTheIssueVolume asserted, for XDG_STATE_HOME among the five, that mountHolding gives the issue volume with SubPath "" and that it overlaps neither LEGION_WORKSPACE nor uv's two. The replacement covers those for the four shared names and the Go pair; XDG_STATE_HOME now appears only in TestEachRolesAgentIsToldAStateHomeOfItsOwn, which asserts the literal value and cross-role distinctness and nothing about mounts. podsafety.go:206 meanwhile still cites the merged test as the fence for 'the rule that these paths sit on the issue volume's own mount', so a reader is told the state home is covered when it is the one that is not. The container is already in hand in that test: adding mountHolding and the overlap loop is a few lines.

Three sites still derive the socket-length fence from a path this change no longer renders. socketpath_test.go:13 and :38-39, shim_test.go:388-389 and worker_shim_test.go:22 all state that a role container's TMPDIR is `/legion/scratch/<role>/tmp`, 31 bytes for the implementer; it is `/legion/scratch/tmp`, 19. socketpath_test.go:16 then builds its fixture from `const want = len("/legion/scratch/implementer/tmp")`. The fence is harmless — 31 is stricter than 19 — but its stated derivation is false, so the next reader cannot tell whether 31 is a deliberate margin or a stale copy, and cannot re-derive the real headroom. This is distinct from the carried fast-follow, which is about the other copies of the helper rather than the reason written into this one.

The replacement reason this branch gave CheckPod's /home/legion/.local/state row is itself false, and that row is now vestigial. It reads that 'an operator's mount there would still put its volume where workspace-init keeps the XDG state it provisions the issue under'. An operator's mounts never reach an init container: r.pod.VolumeMounts is concatenated only into the role containers (manifest.go:470) and the image probe's (probe.go:835), and a repository-wide grep finds no third site. So the refusal guards nothing it now names. The refusal itself is harmless and the path is worth reserving; either drop the row or keep it as deliberate reserve-the-name hardening and say that, rather than attributing it to a container the rule cannot reach. This continues the round-2 thread I closed as fixed: the owner it was given is not reachable by the thing being fenced.

thermonuclear.deepReview: Six findings. Carried: the bun cold-fill race (which I then reproduced myself), the Playwright sizing misattribution, the stale non-test comments, the claude-envoy changelog, and the operatorpod row. Not carried: the PR body's Look at first line, which is mine and which I rewrote at this head. Its negatives are the valuable half and are recorded: the claude-bridge inbox socket is not a Sandbox shape at all (config/backends.go refuses `claude` under runtime: kubernetes, and the socket is os.MkdirTemp-unique even under tmux); Playwright's install is serialized by a mkdir-based directory lock at <registry>/__dirlock with a ~10-minute back-off, and the issue's one checkout means its .links registry cannot GC a sibling's browser; the only fixed name found under the shared TMPDIR is codegraph's node-compile-cache, keyed by node version, arch, source hash and uid, which eight concurrent runs filled with identical content and zero failures; no per-role secret is in the scratch, every one staying on its own volume under /var/run/legion; and Oh My Pi's own data- and cache-class directories stay at /home/legion/.omp because it honours those variables only where the profile directory already exists.
thermonuclear.codeQuality: Seven findings. Carried: the worker_shim comment, the Playwright sizing line, the three socket-length sites and the merged test's lost assertion. Not carried as findings: the XDG_DATA_HOME profile-root relocation, which is latent rather than live and is in the body's risk list instead (nothing creates $XDG_DATA_HOME/omp and EnsureScratch makes the bare root only; what the change alters is that the path it would point at is now shared and persistent); the rationale duplicated across about fifteen sites, which is real and is the carried scratch.go extraction's to collapse rather than relocate; and the merged test's [][2]string table, which is style. It confirms the mechanism independently: roleEnvironment renders the four shared names off scratchRoot and the pair off the Go consts, roleStateHome is the only per-role value, roleScratch has no caller left, runtimeOwned and the controller's told-variable list carry the four names, and launcherRoles includes the controller so the merged test covers the container it claims to.

closingRound.standard: The architect set rounds three and four as closing rounds: approve when the previous findings are answered and what remains is of the fast-follow class, and let a new finding earn the round only if it is a defect of this change. He named XDG_STATE_HOME as the one thing that must not be shared and said he would back a finding there.
closingRound.applied: XDG_STATE_HOME is still the role's own and its reason survives in an executable test, so that one is clear. The bun cold-fill race is the second thing that must not be shared, found by the fixed-name and concurrency hunt rather than by the rule, and it breaks the daemon's own install rather than only a statement: it is the round, and it is the 'genuinely must not ship' case the architect reserved. The five others travel with it at no extra cost, three of them statements the inversion left standing. Nothing in the round questions the human's decision or the direction.
